properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::shortest_path (unused) returns the actual Path between two nodes. Two readings on a design graph:
(a) surprising_connections reports that two things bridge separate communities. It does not say through what. The path is the explanation a human needs before acting.
(b) "Why is this node in my blast radius?" propagate reports hop distance and impact direction; a named path is the artifact a person can read and check.

CHEAP: exact, already a dependency, and both call sites already hold the network.

WHERE IT LANDS: this is the BL-114 family again from a third direction — a finding that states a conclusion without stating the evidence it walked. BL-141(a) has just done exactly this for circular_dependency (name the contracts the cycle ran through), and that change was small and immediately useful on real data. The same argument applies here.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a shortest path is not necessarily the RESPONSIBLE path — several may exist, and showing one implies a causal story that may not be the operative one. BL-141(a) sidestepped this by naming the SET of contracts involved rather than a single route; the equivalent here might be "the edge types this coupling runs through" rather than one path. Worth deciding which before building.
properties.name: OPEN — should a finding say HOW two nodes are coupled, not only that they are?
properties.rationale: Grouped with the explain-what-you-walked family (BL-114, BL-141a) rather than presented as a new idea, because that is what it is — the third instance of the same shape.
